clue.text: TV show where couples dance, preferring tango to waltz originally

indicators.note: preferring one thing to another means putting the first in the second's place, so one letter swaps out for another

parts.note: taken as written, before its first letter is swapped
Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: originally points to how a word starts, so only its opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the letter that is pushed out
couples are pairs
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Describes a ballroom dancing show where couples favour the tango over the waltz.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a dance-show answer like Strictly; in fact WHERE becomes THERE once T replaces W, then THERE PAIRS HOP reads as THE REPAIR SHOP. The Repair Shop is a BBC programme in which craftspeople restore treasured objects.
explanation.definitionFit: The Repair Shop is a long-running British television programme about restoring heirlooms, so it is a TV show.

clue.text: Focus on procedure regularly aiming for improved accuracy

parts.note: to target is to focus on
a practice is an established procedure

explanation.surface: Advice to concentrate on method when training regularly to become more accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the first word above the second in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Target practice is repeated shooting at a target to make a marksman more accurate.

clue.text: Leaves survive when temperature is higher

indicators.note: in a down entry higher means further up, so that letter is lifted out and slotted in at an earlier point

parts.note: to exist is to survive; its final letter is taken off
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Suggests foliage that lives on in a warmer climate.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the T of EXIST up one place and it becomes EXITS. 'Leaves' looks like foliage but is the noun for ways out.
explanation.definitionFit: Exits are ways out or departures, matching the plural noun leaves as in takes leave.

clue.text: Following lead, maybe at intervals fairly simple?

parts.note: lead is one example of a chemical element

indicators.note: at intervals means every so often, so alternate letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Wonders whether taking the lead now and then is reasonably easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the alternate letters after the element; 'lead' is the metal, not leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means basic and easy, as in Holmes's 'Elementary, my dear Watson'.

clue.text: Rampant disease no menace to house plant

indicators.note: rampant describes an animal rearing up on its hind legs, so in this down entry the letters read upwards
to house something is to hold it inside, so the answer is sitting within the run of words

parts.note: letters running across the word breaks, from the end of the first word to the middle of the last

explanation.surface: Reassures that a spreading illness poses no threat to a pot plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house plant' looks like the definition, but 'house' belongs with 'to' as the hiding signal, leaving just 'plant'.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone, or windflower, is a flowering plant of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Bicycle, one that Elizabeth admired

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a famous British bicycle brand
second meaning: a favourite courtier of Queen Elizabeth I

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Walter Raleigh was a courtier and explorer famously favoured by Elizabeth I; Raleigh is also a long-established Nottingham cycle maker.
explanation.definitionFit: The same surname names both a bicycle manufacturer and the Elizabethan adventurer the queen favoured.

clue.text: Great quantity of spirit, with gallons discounted

indicators.note: something discounted is left out of the reckoning, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a ghost is a spirit
G is the abbreviation for gallons

explanation.surface: A lot of liquor sold cheap by the gallon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests alcohol, fitting gallons, but it is a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a large number of people or things, as in a host of admirers.

clue.text: Articulate and extremely capable, she perhaps is superior

indicators.note: superior means placed above, so in this down entry that piece is written on top

parts.note: she is an example of a pronoun

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes or ends of a word, so only its outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: Praises a woman who speaks clearly, is very able and outranks others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' looks like an adjective, but the answer is the verb, to speak clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to articulate, that is, to say a word clearly and correctly.

clue.text: Lying about time in posh hotel flusters nun terribly

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, here inside the posh hotel pair
terribly means very badly, so the letters are thrown into a different order

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the letters to be rearranged
U means upper-class

explanation.surface: A tale about a nun badly flustered during her stay in a smart hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: T in UH, plus the letters of 'flusters nun', all rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Untruthfulness is the quality or act of telling falsehoods, which is what lying is.

clue.text: When rioting her allies cause much trouble

indicators.note: rioting suggests disorder, so the letters run wild into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman's friends make a nuisance of themselves when they take part in a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise hell is an idiom for creating a great disturbance or making a fuss.

clue.text: Court before long will restrict parking

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: before long means soon
P is the standard abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Suggests a court case where parking is about to be limited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court but is the verb, to woo; P goes inside SOON to give SPOON.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoon is an old-fashioned word for to kiss and cuddle romantically, close in sense to courting a sweetheart.

clue.text: Come after son, breaking sequence occasionally on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the kept letters are read the other way round
breaking into a sequence means getting inside it, so one piece sits within the other
occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Reads like a description of a child who follows on and disrupts an orderly series.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on afterwards, especially as a result, so it means to come after.

clue.text: Greeting bespectacled Pennsylvanian neighbour

indicators.note: wearing spectacles means having lenses round the eyes, so a pair of round letters frame the greeting

parts.note: a pair of spectacles is drawn as two rings
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: Pictures saying hello to a glasses-wearing person living next door in Pennsylvania.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords often draw spectacles as two round letters, like a pair of lenses.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohio is the US state on Pennsylvania's western border, so it is that state's neighbour.

clue.text: Competition giving away celebrity books and pleasure trip

indicators.note: giving something away means losing it, so these pieces are removed from the longer word

parts.note: a tournament is a competition
a big name is a celebrity
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A contest that hands out a famous author's books along with a holiday as prizes.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove NAME and then NT from TOURNAMENT and only TOUR is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour is a journey for pleasure visiting several places, such as a holiday excursion.

clue.text: Moneymaking ability criminal admits with pained expression

indicators.note: criminal means crooked or bent, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
ouch is what one says when hurt

explanation.surface: A crook grudgingly confesses his talent for making money, wincing as he does so.
explanation.definitionFit: The Midas touch, from the Greek king who turned everything to gold, is a knack for making money.

clue.text: Help Rita briefly after mixing potion

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the name is dropped
mixing stirs things together, so the letters come out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
the name without its last letter

explanation.surface: Asks for a quick hand for Rita once a potion has been stirred up.
explanation.definitionFit: A philtre is a magic drink, especially a love potion, so it is a kind of potion.

clue.text: Improper behaviour during last month over drink

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
Dec is December, the last month of the year
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
rum is a drink

explanation.surface: Describes bad conduct at a December party fuelled by alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is a lack of decorum, that is, conduct that breaks the rules of propriety.

clue.text: Shock coverage of German gentleman broadcast, facing capture

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: Herr is the German for Mr, a gentleman's title
to net is to capture

explanation.surface: Sounds like a startling news report about a German man about to be caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' is not surprise but a shock of hair, a thick mass, so the definition is something that covers hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairnet is a fine mesh worn over the hair to hold it in place, so it covers a shock of hair.

clue.text: Alternative options presented to soldiers in country

parts.note: and/or offers either option or both
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Sounds like a menu of choices put to troops stationed in a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative options' is the written form and/or, which offers one, the other or both.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a small independent principality in the Pyrenees between France and Spain.

clue.text: Upset old lady penning article is creating disbelief

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so the other pieces sit inside
in a down entry upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
the definite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: An agitated old woman writes an essay that leaves readers unconvinced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old lady' means mother, not an elderly woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheism is the absence of belief in any god, so it is a form of religious disbelief.

clue.text: Duck farmer initially seizes each person found stealing

indicators.note: to seize something is to grab hold of it, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: a teal is a small duck

indicators.note: initially points to the start, so only the farmer's first letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter
ea is the usual abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: A farmer grabs a duck from every thief he catches on his land.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea leaf is Cockney rhyming slang for thief.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a tea leaf rhymes with thief, so it names someone caught stealing.

clue.text: Inscription on gift for Daisy, possibly electrical appliance?

wordplay.note: a gift tag reading 'to' plus a flower name, since a daisy is an aster

explanation.surface: A gift tag for someone called Daisy, perhaps attached to a kitchen gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: A tag reads 'To' plus the recipient; Daisy is taken as the flower, and the daisy belongs to the aster family, so TO ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A toaster is a common electric kitchen device for browning slices of bread.

clue.text: Remains undressed for moment

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of outer clothing, so the outside letters are removed

parts.note: something that sticks remains in place

explanation.surface: Suggests a body left unclothed for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is British slang for a very short time, as in 'just a tick', so it is a moment.

clue.text: Stop doctors' adviser attending operation essentially

parts.note: WHO is the World Health Organization, which advises doctors worldwide

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or heart of a word, so only its central letter is taken

parts.note: the middle letter of the nine

explanation.surface: Sounds like a halt called to a consultant who is present at surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is a command to stop, originally used to halt a horse.

clue.text: Drier patch of ground westwards we must occupy

indicators.note: to occupy a space is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other
in an across clue westwards means right to left, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lot is a plot of land
taken as written

explanation.surface: A settler's instruction to take over a drier piece of land out west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drier' looks like the comparative of dry; it is the noun, a thing that dries.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel is a cloth used to dry yourself, so it is a drier.

clue.text: Delays works inside cafe?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: holds back before acting
second meaning: serves tables as a job

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that cafe work is only one place the second sense applies.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait is both to hold off or delay and to serve customers at table in a restaurant.

clue.text: Free to sack the French solicitor

indicators.note: to sack someone is to dismiss them, so those letters are thrown out of the phrase

parts.note: to let out is to free
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Suggests the French being free to dismiss their lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like a lawyer, a British term, but it is the literal sense: someone who solicits custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A tout is someone who solicits business, such as a ticket tout pestering buyers.

clue.text: Load vehicle then depart

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to go is to depart

explanation.surface: Instructions to pack a car before setting off.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is goods carried by a ship, plane or vehicle, that is, its load.

clue.text: Current unrest erupts, involving four becoming pushy

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the number goes inside the shuffled letters
an eruption throws things about violently, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Present-day disorder breaks out among a group of four, making them aggressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone intrusive pushes into matters that are not theirs, so the word describes a pushy person.

clue.text: Work by Ovid, poem some trash unusually

indicators.note: unusually means in an odd way, so the letters are set out in an unexpected order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses one of Ovid's poems as unusually poor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Metamorphoses is Ovid's long Latin narrative poem of mythological transformations.
